profile.name: Digital twin adherence
profile.description: Measures how strongly the supplied evidence supports the functional characteristics of a digital twin.
profile.instruction: Judge only capabilities explicitly supported by the supplied evidence.

criteria.instructions: Does the evidence clearly show a digital representation of one specific, identifiable physical or biological counterpart, rather than a generic model?
Does measured data from that specific counterpart initialize or personalize its corresponding model?
Is the virtual representation repeatedly updated with new data from the same real-world counterpart?
Does the virtual representation simulate scenarios, predict outcomes, or evaluate interventions?
Does the company explicitly call this product or technology a digital twin?
Even if a complete digital twin is not evidenced, is this clearly an enabling component such as virtual modeling, simulation, sensing, or data integration?

profile.name: GSD patient-journey de-para mapping
profile.description: Measures whether the supplied evidence supports at least one concrete functional de-para from an existing solution to an education, longitudinal-information, or care-continuity need in the glycogen storage disease patient journey. Auxiliary criteria identify the non-exclusive destination categories and contextualize how directly the solution already addresses GSD or adjacent conditions.
profile.instruction: Evaluate functional de-para potential, not literal disease adherence. Judge only capabilities explicitly demonstrated by the supplied evidence. Count a capability when its documented user, workflow, and information function materially match a defined need in the glycogen storage disease patient journey, even if the solution was built for another disease or population. Do not require or reward GSD terminology by itself. Do not infer missing product functions, operational availability, clinical validity, regulatory suitability, interoperability, or configurability from branding, generic claims, or plausibility.

criteria.instructions: Does the evidence demonstrate at least one operational solution capability with a concrete functional de-para to an education, longitudinal-information, or care-continuity need in the GSD patient journey?
Does the evidenced solution capability map to delivering structured health education to patients or caregivers?
Does the evidenced solution capability map to delivering clinical education or training to healthcare professionals?
Does the evidenced solution capability map to maintaining and retrieving a patient-level clinical history across time?
Does the evidenced solution capability map to coordinating handoffs, referrals, tasks, or next steps across a patient's care journey?
Does the evidenced solution capability map to helping a patient or caregiver carry out and document an ongoing care routine?
Does the evidenced solution capability map to repeatedly collecting patient-level status or outcome information for follow-up?
Does the evidenced solution capability map to creating, delivering, managing, or tracking a patient-specific prescription or care plan?
Does the evidenced solution capability map to making essential patient information or care instructions available during an emergency or care transition?
Does the evidence show that the mapped capability is currently available in an operational product or service rather than only proposed, planned, or described generically?
Does the evidence explicitly state that the solution supports glycogen storage disease or people affected by it?
Does the evidence explicitly place the solution in a rare-disease or inherited-metabolic-disease care context other than glycogen storage disease?
Does the evidence explicitly show that the solution can be configured for different diseases or care pathways?

Count a capability when its documented user, workflow, and information function materially match a defined need in the glycogen storage disease patient journey, even if the solution was built for another disease or population. Do not require or reward GSD terminology by itself. Do not infer missing product functions, operational availability, clinical validity, regulatory suitability, interoperability, or configurability from branding, generic claims, or plausibility.

criteria.instructions: Does the evidence demonstrate at least one operational solution capability with a concrete functional de-para to an education, longitudinal-information, or care-continuity need in the GSD patient journey?
Does the evidenced solution capability map to delivering structured health education to patients or caregivers?
Does the evidenced solution capability map to delivering clinical education or training to healthcare professionals?
Does the evidenced solution capability map to maintaining and retrieving a patient-level clinical history across time?
Does the evidenced solution capability map to coordinating handoffs, referrals, tasks, or next steps across a patient's care journey?
Does the evidenced solution capability map to helping a patient or caregiver carry out and document an ongoing care routine?
Does the evidenced solution capability map to repeatedly collecting patient-level status or outcome information for follow-up?
Does the evidenced solution capability map to creating, delivering, managing, or tracking a patient-specific prescription or care plan?
Does the evidenced solution capability map to making essential patient information or care instructions available during an emergency or care transition?
Does the evidence show that the mapped capability is currently available in an operational product or service rather than only proposed, planned, or described generically?
Does the evidence explicitly state that the solution supports glycogen storage disease or people affected by it?
Does the evidence explicitly place the solution in a rare-disease or inherited-metabolic-disease care context other than glycogen storage disease?
Does the evidence explicitly show that the solution can be configured for different diseases or care pathways?
